name_en: Ibara mochi — sweet rice cake wrapped in smilax leaves
summary_ja: 上新粉の生地であんを包み、丸くつるりとしたサルトリイバラの葉で包んで蒸した5月の節句菓子。津市では「いばら餅」、地域によって「がんだち餅」「どっかん餅」などと呼び名が変わると伝わる。
summary_en: Sweet bean paste wrapped in rice-flour dough is enclosed in a round, smooth smilax leaf and steamed, traditionally made for the May boy's festival. Known as "ibara mochi" in Tsu, the same treat carries different names — "gandachi mochi," "dokkan mochi" — across other parts of Mie.

name_en: Naisho mochi — half-pounded rice cake made quietly without a mortar
summary_ja: 蒸したもち米とうるち米を鍋の中で半づきにし、よもぎとあんを混ぜて仕上げる大台町の餅菓子。臼と杵を使う音が近所に響くのを避け、内緒でつくったことが名の由来とされ、「なべ餅」とも呼ばれる。
summary_en: Steamed glutinous and non-glutinous rice are half-pounded together in a pot, then finished with mugwort and sweet bean paste, a specialty of Odai town. The name, meaning "secret mochi," is said to come from making it quietly in a pot rather than with a mortar and pestle, whose thumping would carry to the neighbors; it is also called "nabe mochi."
source_title: ないしょ餅/なべ餅 三重県
